headline_marked: Mymensingh hospital fire: [[Reports of 6 stampede deaths incorrect]], says commissioner
headline: Mymensingh hospital fire: Reports of 6 stampede deaths incorrect, says commissioner
summary: Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar clarifies that no one died in a stampede after a fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital.
details: A fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) around 6:00 PM on Monday, causing panic among patients and attendants as smoke spread across multiple floors.
Several people were injured while rushing downstairs to escape the smoke. Ten fire service units from five stations were deployed to bring the blaze under control by 6:30 PM.
Following the incident, reports circulated claiming six people had died in a stampede. However, Mymensingh Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar has dismissed these reports as false.
The commissioner explained that after verifying hospital records and the morgue, the administration found that one person listed as dead was actually alive, and two others had died of natural causes.
He confirmed that while there were injuries due to the rush and panic, the Fire Service and local administration have verified that no deaths occurred as a result of a stampede.
The fire is suspected to have been caused by an electrical short circuit in a non-operational lift, though a full investigation is underway to determine the exact cause.
caption:
Reports of 6 deaths in a stampede at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital have been debunked by the divisional commissioner.

A fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) around 6:00 PM on Monday, causing panic among patients and attendants as smoke spread across multiple floors.

Several people were injured while rushing downstairs to escape the smoke. Ten fire service units from five stations were deployed to bring the blaze under control by 6:30 PM.

Following the incident, reports circulated claiming six people had died in a stampede. However, Mymensingh Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar has dismissed these reports as false.

The commissioner explained that after verifying hospital records and the morgue, the administration found that one person listed as dead was actually alive, and two others had died of natural causes.

He confirmed that while there were injuries due to the rush and panic, the Fire Service and local administration have verified that no deaths occurred as a result of a stampede.

The fire is suspected to have been caused by an electrical short circuit in a non-operational lift, though a full investigation is underway to determine the exact cause.

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune

headline_marked: DU students [[rip Jinnah photos]] at Ducsu archive over language movement history
headline: DU students rip Jinnah photos at Ducsu archive over language movement history
summary: Protests erupt at Dhaka University after the Ducsu archive displayed photos of Pakistan's founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah, while removing photos of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.
details: A Dhaka University student ripped three photos of Muhammad Ali Jinnah from the Ducsu archive after the images were displayed following the renovation of the museum.
The controversy began on Sunday night when social media criticism surged after news of the images' inclusion became public.

Students from various political groups, including the Jatiya Chhatra Dal and Bangladesh Chhatra Union, protested the move, calling it a distortion of the history of the language and independence movements.
In a counter-protest, students from the Chhatra Federation displayed a photo of former Jamaat-e-Islami chief Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes at the site where Jinnah's photos were placed.
The archive had also removed single or glorious photos of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, which were previously present, further fueling the student anger.
Ducsu General Secretary SM Farhad claimed the photos were meant to show Jinnah's anti-Bengali language stance, but students argued Jinnah had no place in the Ducsu archive.
Dhaka University administration has formed a probe committee led by Professor Mohammad Almojaddedi Alfechani to investigate the incident.
The committee will also investigate the unauthorized installation of memorials and the launch of a teacher evaluation website without university permission.
